quote: Have a seat, Mr. Ehrmantraut. Did I pronounce that right?
title: Seat and name
comment: The agents take the initiative from the first second: an invitation to sit and a name check. Polite tone, but they own the room.

title: Close enough
comment: Mike won't even confirm the right pronunciation. His first line already sets his plan: not a single spare detail.

quote: So you're waiving your right to have a lawyer present?
title: The lawyer question
comment: The agents check whether Mike will have cover. If not, everything he says next goes on the record without counsel.

title: A flat 'right'
comment: One word instead of explanations. Mike doesn't justify the waiver, so he doesn't signal he has anything to hide.

quote: Say that for the camera, please.
title: Waiver on tape
comment: The waiver has to be repeated on video: that makes it legally clean and leaves Mike no way back.

quote: I waive my right to have a lawyer present.
title: Lawyer sacrifice
comment: Mike gives up his main defensive piece on purpose. Simple math: silence without a lawyer is more convincing than talk with one.

quote: You're employed by the Los Pollos Hermanos restaurant chain, is that correct?
title: The official cover
comment: A procedural question that pins down Mike's cover. Later the agents will check his words against the facts.

title: Head of security
comment: The job title, no details. Mike gives exactly what the agents already know and nothing more.

quote: So, what, you guard the secret sauce?
title: Sauce jab
comment: A jab instead of a question. It brings no information and shows irritation, while Mike answers in an even tone.

quote: I run background checks on employees and prevent losses.
title: Boring truth
comment: A dry, believable answer. It defuses the mockery without an argument and gives no hook for the next question.

quote: And the fast food place is your only job?
title: Only job?
comment: The agents look for a second income. If there is one, Mike's cover story cracks.

quote: We have fourteen locations, so yes, there's no other.
title: Fourteen locations
comment: A chain of fourteen sounds solid and dull. The answer closes the question with nothing to pick at.
